name: Inna and Babies
description: Inna, Dima and Sereja are in one room together. It's cold outside, so Sereja suggested to play a board game called "Babies". The babies playing board is an infinite plane containing n blue babies and m red ones. Each baby is a segment that grows in time. At time moment t the blue baby ( x , y ) is a blue segment with ends at points ( x - t , y + t ) , ( x + t , y - t ) . Similarly, at time t the red baby ( x , y ) is a red segment with ends at points ( x + t , y + t ) , ( x - t , y - t ) of the plane. Initially, at time t = 0 all babies are points on the plane. The goal of the game is to find the first integer moment of time when the plane contains a rectangle of a non-zero area which sides are fully covered by some babies. A side may be covered by multiple babies. More formally, each point of each side of the rectangle should be covered by at least one baby of any color. At that, you must assume that the babies are closed segments, that is, they contain their endpoints. You are given the positions of all babies — help Inna and Dima to find the required moment of time.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n , m ≤ 2000) . Next n lines contain the coordinates of the blue babies. The i -th line contains integers x i , y i — a baby's coordinates. Next m lines contain the coordinates of m red babies in the similar form. All coordinates of the input don't exceed 10 6 in their absolute value. Note that all babies stand in distinct points.
output_specification: In the single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem. If the rectangle never appears on the plane, print " Poor Sereja! " without the quotes.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 374E — Inna and Babies [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
